exercises.approach: Call plot on d$x and d$y with xlab, ylab and main set, so the high level call opens the page and fixes the coordinates.
exercises.why: The five pairs (0, 0) through (4, 8) are the measured quantities, and naming the axes Input value and Response value tells a reader which is which before any rule is drawn.
exercises.wrong: Starting with points or abline on a fresh device. Low level functions need an existing plot, so R stops with plot.new has not been called yet.
exercises.verify: `all(d$y == 2 * d$x)` returns TRUE, and the device shows five filled points with both axis titles.

exercises.approach: Add the rule with abline(a = 0, b = 2) on the same plot.
exercises.why: abline draws in the coordinates plot already set, so the line from (0, 0) to (4, 8) passes through every observed pair. That agreement is visible because the data were generated as y = 2x.
exercises.wrong: Drawing the rule with a second plot call such as `plot(d$x, 2 * d$x, type = "l")`. That opens a new page, so the points disappear and the line is never compared with them.
exercises.verify: The device shows one line passing through all five points on a single panel.

exercises.approach: Pass xlim = c(0, 4), ylim = c(0, 8) together with xaxs = "i" and yaxs = "i", then read par("usr").
exercises.why: The "i" style uses the limits exactly, so the plotting region runs from 0 to 4 across and 0 to 8 up, which is what the coordinate check expects.
exercises.wrong: Setting the limits but keeping the default "r" style. R then pads each range by 4 percent, so usr becomes about -0.16 to 4.16 and -0.32 to 8.32, and an exact comparison fails.

exercises.approach: Order the rows by time with `unsorted[order(unsorted$time), ]` before passing them to lines.
exercises.why: lines joins points in the order supplied. The rows arrive as times 3, 1 and 2, so the path would run from time 3 back to 1 and then forward to 2, which is not a trajectory.
exercises.wrong: Trusting the picture to reveal the problem. These three values sit exactly on value = 10 times time, so the backtracking path overlaps itself and looks like a clean line; only the order check exposes it.

exercises.approach: Open png on a tempfile, record its device number, register cleanup with on.exit, draw, call dev.off, and only then read the first 8 bytes.
exercises.why: The PNG is complete only after dev.off. Its first bytes, 137 80 78 71 13 10 26 10, mark a real PNG file, and the cleanup closes the owned device only if it is still current before removing the file.
exercises.wrong: Reading the bytes before dev.off, which can find an empty or partial file, or cleaning up with graphics.off, which also closes devices the caller opened.
exercises.verify: `readBin(path, "raw", n = 8)` returns the 8 signature bytes inside the function, and `file.exists(removed)` returns FALSE afterward.

exercises.approach: List the three checks separately: assertions on d, the signature and size of the PNG file, and a browser view of the delivered figure.
exercises.why: The assertions confirm y = 2x and the coordinate range. The signature confirms the file is a PNG. Neither says whether the axis labels are legible or the line color is distinguishable on the page.
exercises.wrong: Treating a clean Rscript exit as proof that the figure works for students. The script can pass while labels overlap or the image fails to load in the classroom.
exercises.verify: Running the reference prints r-051 reference checks passed, and a separate browser screenshot shows the labels readable.

run_note: The starter holds five points with x from 0 to 4 and y equal to twice x, and an empty results list. Run it and confirm the rule by eye in the printed frame before drawing. When you set limits of 0 to 4 and 0 to 8, also set `xaxs` and `yaxs` to "i", or base graphics pads each axis and `par("usr")` will not report the limits you asked for.
checks_note: The assertions confirm that the plot region spans exactly 0 to 4 and 0 to 8 and that every y equals twice x, that rows reordered by time give values 10, 20 and 30 in order before a line is drawn, that the owned temporary file starts with the eight byte PNG signature and is not empty, and that the file no longer exists after cleanup. They do not show that a viewer can read the labels.
